title: Founders, operators and the lawyers
lede: Titles follow the sources named in each entry. Where we found no source for a later career, it is left out.

people.name: Marno McDermott
people.text: A University of Minnesota graduate who discovered Mexican food in California, built Zapata Foods and sold it to Heublein for $4M, then opened Chi-Chi’s as a sit-down version.[^1]
people.later: His son Michael revived the name in 2025.[^29]

people.name: Max McGee
people.text: A former Green Bay Packers wide receiver who owned the Left Guard bar and restaurant. Half of it became the first Chi-Chi’s.[^1][^42]

people.name: John Stephens
people.text: A Minneapolis stockbroker who bought the rights to operate and franchise Chi-Chi’s through his publicly traded company.[^1]

people.name: Shelly Frank
people.text: Negotiated Heublein’s purchase of Zapata, then worked on new concepts at Kentucky Fried Chicken. He joined at 33 and moved the headquarters to Louisville.[^1]
people.later: Retired in 1986, by a reference history’s account.[^2]

people.name: Hal Smith
people.text: Came from Chili’s. He cut corporate staff, shortened managers’ hours and stayed on under Foodmaker until he quit in June 1992.[^2]

people.name: Joe Micatrotto
people.text: A long-time Chi-Chi’s employee who became president when Smith’s successor moved on after six months, and who went on to lead Family Restaurants.[^2]

people.name: Kevin S. Relyea
people.role: Chairman and chief executive of Prandium
people.text: Ran the parent through its 2002 Chapter 11 and resigned all his positions on December 30, 2002.[^2][^7]

people.name: Hugh G. Hilton
people.role: Chief executive of Prandium from Feb 2003
people.text: A member of the turnaround firm Alvarez & Marsal, appointed interim chief executive. He signed the filing that reported Chi-Chi’s Chapter 11.[^7][^9]

people.name: Bill Zavertnik
people.text: The company’s voice in the first weeks of the outbreak. He announced that green onions had been removed from every kitchen before the cause was confirmed.[^14]

people.name: Jack Utsick
people.text: An entertainment promoter whose company Worldwide Entertainment was majority owner of the entity that signed a letter of intent for Chi-Chi’s in October 2003.[^9][^15]

people.name: William Marler
people.text: A Seattle lawyer who represented about a third of the claimants and handled the class action for people who received shots.[^20][^23]

people.name: Joseph Kadow
people.text: Explained the purchase: Outback wanted locations, and took no brand, operations or recipes.[^20]

people.name: Francis Leroy
people.text: A Belgian operator who held the Chi-Chi’s rights for Europe, North Africa and Asia in 2014 and spoke of 400 restaurants in Europe.[^40]

people.name: Michael McDermott
people.text: The founder’s son, with a career at Kona Grill and Rojo Mexican Grill. He announced the agreement with Hormel in 2024 and opened the St. Louis Park restaurant in 2025.[^30][^36]
